profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between the epidemiology lead for a multinational pediatric allergy study and the data operations coordinator at a regional implementation hub. They are preparing the handoff from local field teams to the central analysis group for an ISAAC-style Phase 1 survey rollout across six centres in three countries. The immediate context is that the first two centres have nearly finished school-based data collection, and both participants want to align on what local teams should submit, how completion status will be reported, and what materials will be reused later for Phase 3 trend analysis. The agenda is to confirm the weekly status update format, clarify the 'final' questionnaire package to be shared with the analysis group, align on the symptom severity summary that accompanies each centre's upload, and check ownership of the centre-level codebook and translation files. The expected outcome is an apparently smooth agreement on handoffs, timelines, and shared artifacts before the next Friday reporting checkpoint.

members.name: Dr. Lena Varga
members.expertise: Pediatric respiratory epidemiology, cross-centre study standardization, questionnaire-based prevalence studies
members.background: Based at the coordinating university unit, Lena previously worked on multinational child health surveys and now oversees protocol consistency and comparability across participating ISAAC-style centres.
members.private_state: She wants centre submissions to be analysis-ready with minimal back-and-forth because the steering group expects an early cross-country prevalence snapshot next month; she is especially concerned about preserving comparability for later trend analyses.
hidden_assumptions: A centre marked as 'complete' has finished data entry, cleaning, and de-duplication to the point that prevalence tables can be generated without another operational pass.
The 'final questionnaire package' means the exact center-approved instrument set that was actually administered, including locally adapted translations and interviewer notes that affect coding.
A 'severity summary' should follow the ISAAC reporting convention used by the central team: child-level categories derived from symptom questions over the last 12 months, broken out by age group.
The shared codebook is a living central artifact that regional teams update directly when local response labels or translation nuances change.

members.name: Omar Ndlovu
members.expertise: Field logistics, multilingual survey deployment, data capture workflows, school-based study coordination
members.background: Omar manages implementation support for several centres in Southern and Eastern Africa, coordinating school recruitment, translation vendors, data entry contractors, and weekly progress reporting from field supervisors.
members.private_state: He wants to keep field teams moving and avoid reopening nearly completed centres for administrative refinements; he is focused on operational throughput and on showing that centres are on schedule for collection milestones.
hidden_assumptions: A centre reported as 'complete' means all planned schools have finished questionnaire collection, even if entry checks, reconciliation, or coding normalization continue afterward.
The 'final questionnaire package' is the locked master packet approved before fieldwork began, not the exact centre-by-centre set of annotated local variants used on the ground.
A 'severity summary' is a simple centre-level operational snapshot for the weekly deck, typically percentage with any wheeze and counts of severe episodes, aggregated across the whole centre.
Local translation mappings and response label notes are owned by the regional operations folder and only need to be sent centrally if a problem is discovered.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as a centre being complete
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both refer to centres being 'complete' before Friday's checkpoint.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the centre is ready for central analysis: collection finished, data entered, basic cleaning done, duplicates resolved, and missing school identifiers reconciled.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means field collection is finished at all planned schools, regardless of whether data entry cleanup and coding checks are still underway.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In coordination meetings, 'complete' commonly functions as a routine status shorthand; both assume the other shares the obvious operational meaning and neither sees a need to unpack completion criteria unless something goes wrong.

misalignment_points.topic: Which questionnaire package is the final one
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to send the 'final questionnaire package' to the central team.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the actual administered package for each centre, including the last approved translation wording, skip-instruction annotations, and any local wording adjustments preserved for reproducibility.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the pre-fieldwork locked packet stored in the regional deployment folder, which may not include later on-paper clarifications or centre-specific translated refinements used in schools.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are pointing to a single seemingly established object with an authoritative name, so the phrase creates false consensus even though each has a different file set in mind.

misalignment_points.topic: What the severity summary should contain
misalignment_points.surface_form: They discuss attaching a 'severity summary' with each centre upload.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means a standardized analytic summary using ISAAC symptom-derived severity categories over the previous 12 months, separated by age band and questionnaire form.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means a brief operational summary slide with overall centre-level percentages and counts that helps monitor whether severe cases are appearing plausible during fieldwork.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The term sounds technical and settled, and both participants are accustomed to producing summaries; because neither expects disagreement over a routine accompaniment, they do not specify level of aggregation or derivation rules.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that the translation notes and codebook should be kept 'up to date' for Phase 3 reuse.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes regional teams will edit the central master codebook directly as local wording and response mappings stabilize so that one authoritative artifact exists for future trend comparisons.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes regional teams maintain their own local version and send a consolidated export later if central analysts ask, because direct edits to the master would disrupt field operations.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: They agree on the outcome—an up-to-date codebook—but silently import different workflow norms about where edits happen and when synchronization occurs, which feels too mundane to spell out.

turns.inner_thought: I need the first two centres genuinely ready for analysis by Friday, not just nominally closed in the field. The steering group wants an early cross-country prevalence snapshot next month, and I cannot afford another round of chasing basic cleaning, duplicate resolution, or missing school IDs. If we're calling them complete, I want them at the point where my team can generate prevalence tables immediately.
turns.utterance: Thanks for making time, Omar. I just want to make sure the first two centres are complete enough for Friday's central checkpoint and that the handoff materials are lined up properly.

turns.inner_thought: That should be fine. Both pilot centres are essentially done from an operations standpoint once the last scheduled schools finish this week. Data entry tidying can keep running in the background, but for reporting purposes they'll be complete, which keeps the field teams on schedule and avoids reopening anything unnecessary.
turns.utterance: Yes, we should be in good shape. Both pilot centres should be complete this week because all scheduled schools are due to finish collection by Thursday.

turns.inner_thought: Good. If he's saying complete, then I can treat these as analysis-ready. I also need the actual administered materials archived now—each centre's final approved translations, any coding-relevant interviewer notes, the exact package used on the ground—so reproducibility is protected before files start drifting.
turns.utterance: That's great to hear. Could you send the final questionnaire package for both centres with the upload, so the analysts can archive everything once the centres are complete?

turns.inner_thought: Easy enough—the locked master packet is already neatly stored in the regional deployment folder. There were a couple of school-side clarifications during implementation, but those were practical tweaks and not something I see as changing what we submit centrally. No reason to complicate the handoff.
turns.utterance: Absolutely. The final questionnaire package is already organized in the regional deployment folder, and there are only a couple of school-side clarifications that shouldn't affect submission.

turns.inner_thought: I also need a proper ISAAC-style severity summary with each upload—derived child-level categories over the last 12 months, separated by age band and questionnaire form—so the steering group can look at early patterns in a format comparable across centres. If that comes in with the questionnaire files, we can move quickly.
turns.utterance: Perfect. I'd also like each centre upload to include a severity summary, so the steering group can review the early prevalence pattern alongside the questionnaire files.

turns.inner_thought: That's straightforward. We already do a simple one-pager for weekly monitoring—overall wheeze percentage plus severe-case counts at the centre level. That should satisfy the request without asking teams for extra analysis work while they're still closing out schools.
turns.utterance: No problem. I can have the team add the usual one-page severity summary with overall wheeze percentages and severe-case counts for each centre.

turns.inner_thought: Good, and I need us not to lose the translation trail. For Phase 3 reuse and later trend comparisons, the central master codebook should keep absorbing local wording refinements and response-label nuances as they stabilize. If regional teams keep it up to date directly, we avoid fragmented documentation later.
turns.utterance: And looking a bit ahead to Phase 3, it will really help if the translation notes and codebook stay up to date as the centres close out.

turns.inner_thought: Yes, the coordinators have been maintaining those materials in the regional operations folders, which is the least disruptive way to support fieldwork. We can always send a consolidated version later if central asks. The important thing is that the files are current locally so nothing stalls on the ground.
turns.utterance: Agreed, that's important. My coordinators have been keeping the local language mappings in their regional operations folders, so those files are staying up to date.

turns.inner_thought: Excellent—then as soon as a centre is uploaded, my team should be able to run the first cross-centre tables immediately. I am counting on complete meaning no further operational pass is needed before prevalence generation. If Friday lands cleanly, we can show the steering group something tangible next month.
turns.utterance: Good. Once a centre is complete and uploaded, my team will start generating the first cross-centre tables right away.

turns.inner_thought: That timing works from my side because the field teams don't need to wait for all the back-office reconciliation to finish before moving on. We'll mark a centre complete when collection is done, push the package, and let entry staff clear the last minor issues afterward while the next schools proceed.
turns.utterance: That works well for us too, because the field teams can move on to the next schools while back-office entry staff finish minor reconciliation after completion.

turns.inner_thought: All right, this sounds settled. By Friday I expect two analysis-ready centres, the exact administered questionnaire materials, standardized severity outputs, and a centrally current codebook trail for future trend work. If all that arrives, the central group can move without another coordination loop.
turns.utterance: So just to summarize: by Friday I'm expecting complete centres, the final questionnaire package, and the severity summary with each upload, and the codebook should remain current for future rounds.

turns.inner_thought: That's manageable. We'll close the centres once the last schools finish, post the locked package, and keep our updated regional files in order. This keeps the teams moving and still gives central what they need for the checkpoint without dragging us back into local cleanup details.
turns.utterance: Understood. I'll have the team deliver everything on Friday and post the package and the updated files once the centres are marked complete.
